subject: Measuring, diagnosing, budgeting, and improving performance — latency, throughput, Core Web Vitals, database queries,…

evals.prompt: Define performance-engineering in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the performance-engineering skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind performance-engineering. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.
A user asks: "design logs, spans, metrics, and correlation IDs before implementation". Should performance-engineering activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force performance-engineering onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to api-design, data-modeling, refactor, observability-modeling, testing-strategy, error-tracking, code-review, connection-pooling.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "profile this slow dashboard and decide what to optimize first". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying performance-engineering.

Place performance-engineering among its adjacent skills (api-design, data-modeling, refactor, observability-modeling, testing-strategy, error-tracking, code-review, connection-pooling). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about performance-engineering and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
